It is submitted that the petitioner no. 2 implicated only for the reason that he is the proprietor of the M/s Sahil Traders and wife of petitioner no. 1.
5

Learned APP duly assisted by learned counsel for the informant while opposing the prayer of bail submitted that the petitioners cheated complainant by not delivering the goods after receiving the payment.

6. In view of aforesaid factual submission and by taking note of fact as dispute primarily appears civil in nature arising out of business dispute, coupled with the fact that complaint in issue not appears supported by Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.70763 of 2024(5) dt.04-02-2026 affidavit,
accordingly both above-named petitioners, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the court below within a period of four weeks, are directed to be released on bail, furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned CJM, Motihari, East Champaran /concerned Court, where the case is pending in connection with Complaint Case No. 2113 of 2019, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C/Section 482(2) of BNSS.
(Chandra Shekhar Jha, J.) S.Tripathi/-
